_meta.indication: POMBILITI, in combination with Opfolda (an enzyme stabilizer), is indicated for the treatment of adult patients with late-onset Pompe disease (GAA deficiency) weighing ≥ 40 kg and who are not improving on their current enzyme replacement therapy (ERT).

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, active-controlled, international, multi-center trial; patients randomized 2:1 to POMBILITI (20 mg/kg IV) plus Opfolda versus a non-U.S.-approved alglucosidase alfa product with placebo, every other week for 52 weeks.
pivotal_trials.population: Adult patients (≥ 18 years) with late-onset Pompe disease (LOPD); 95 (77%) ERT-experienced and 28 (23%) ERT-naive.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Primary efficacy endpoint was change from baseline to Week 52 in the 6-minute walk test (6MWT) to measure functional endurance.
pivotal_trials.n: 123 randomized patients (85 treated with POMBILITI+Opfolda; 38 treated with comparator+placebo)
pivotal_trials.result: Primary endpoint (6MWD change to Week 52): estimated treatment difference 5.3 meters (95% CI -15.2 to 25.9) favoring POMBILITI+Opfolda, driven by the treatment-experienced subgroup (16.1 meters; 95% CI -1.3, 33.4). Key secondary endpoint sitting FVC (% predicted): treatment difference 2.3% (95% CI 0.02 to 4.6).

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (≥ 5%) are headache, diarrhea, fatigue, nausea, abdominal pain, and pyrexia. Serious risks include life-threatening hypersensitivity reactions/anaphylaxis (41 [27%] of POMBILITI-treated patients experienced hypersensitivity reactions) and infusion-associated reactions (48 [32%] patients). Serious adverse reactions in ≥2 patients were anaphylaxis and urticaria.
target_moa: Pompe disease is caused by deficiency of lysosomal acid alpha-glucosidase (GAA), which degrades glycogen to glucose in the lysosome; deficiency leads to intra-lysosomal glycogen accumulation. Cipaglucosidase alfa-atga provides an exogenous source of GAA; its bis-M6P mediates high-affinity binding to M6P receptors, is internalized into lysosomes, and undergoes proteolytic cleavage/N-glycan trimming to the mature active form.
modality: Enzyme (recombinant human GAA / hydrolytic lysosomal glycogen-specific enzyme) for enzyme replacement therapy, co-administered with the small-molecule stabilizer miglustat.

boxed_warning.content: Boxed warning for severe hypersensitivity reactions (including anaphylaxis), infusion-associated reactions (IARs), and risk of acute cardiorespiratory failure in susceptible patients.

advisory_committee.vote: No advisory committee was held for this application; it did not raise challenging efficacy or safety issues that needed external input.

summary.text: BLA 761204 for cipaglucosidase alfa-atga (co-administered with miglustat/NDA 215211) received standard review with major amendment. The product received orphan drug designation (September 2017) and breakthrough therapy designation for LOPD (February 2019). Approval was based on one adequate and well-controlled trial (ATB200-03) with confirmatory evidence; it was not an accelerated approval and no advisory committee was held.

Substantial evidence of effectiveness for cipaglucosidase alfa coadministered with miglustat in patients with LOPD was established using data from one adequate and well-controlled trial with confirmatory evidence (CE).

requirement.text: 4322-1 To perform extractables/leachables studies and risk assessments to evaluate leachables from the container closure system(s) and manufacturing product contact surfaces of cipaglucosidase alfa drug substance and drug product and assess the potential impact of leachables on product quality at the end of drug product shelf-life. Final Report Submission: 12/2023

citations.quote: 4322-1 To perform extractables/leachables studies and risk assessments to evaluate leachables from the container closure system(s) and manufacturing product contact surfaces of cipaglucosidase alfa drug substance and drug product and assess the potential impact of leachables on product quality at the end of drug product shelf-life. The analyses will be performed using drug substance and drug product lot(s) and/or representative samples (b)(4), if justified) analyzed at appropriate time points, including at the end of drug product shelf life. Appropriate methods will be used to detect, identify, and quantify organic non-volatile, volatile and semi-volatile species, and metals. Characterization of the potential impact of leachables on product quality will be assessed using adequate analytical methods. Complete data and the risk evaluation for the potential impact of leachables on product safety and quality will be provided in the final study report per 21 CFR 601.12.

requirement.text: 4322-2 To develop, validate, and implement a test method with justified numerical acceptance criteria for control of cipaglucosidase alfa kinetic parameters during drug product release and stability testing. Final Report Submission: 06/2024

citations.quote: 4322-2 To develop, validate, and implement a test method with justified numerical acceptance criteria for control of cipaglucosidase alfa kinetic parameters during drug product release and stability testing. Critical kinetic parameters (e.g., K_m, K_{cat}, etc.,) will be determined, justified, and included in the control strategy. If applicable, justification and data supporting (b)(4) will be provided. The method validation report for the enzyme kinetic assay, the revised drug product release and stability specifications, and all supporting studies and data will be provided in a final study report per 21 CFR 601.12.
